User

wait, i thought n8n can execute in parallel, am i confusing it with a different tool like make or zapier?

Assistant

I’ll check n8n’s documentation to distinguish branch execution from concurrent workflow runs.

Assistant

You’re right that n8n can run work concurrently. My earlier wording was too broad. There are two distinct behaviors:

Situation n8n behavior
Two branches within one workflow execution Normally completes one branch before starting the other.
Separate workflow executions Can run concurrently, subject to hosting and concurrency limits.

Sources: branch execution order, concurrent executions.

For our demo, we can have document follow-up and brief preparation running concurrently by putting them in separate sub-workflows and launching each with Wait for Sub-Workflow Completion disabled. The parent can then continue while each runs. Execute Sub-workflow documentation

That changes the synchronization design: we need an explicit way to collect both completion results before saving shared CSV updates. A Merge node in the parent wouldn’t, by itself, wait for those detached workflows to finish.

So you aren’t necessarily confusing n8n with another tool—the distinction is branching within one execution versus concurrent executions.

  • Client information

User

thats a pretty big dataset, no?

Assistant

For the two-record demo, it’s tiny. At production scale, yes—loading all four CSVs and duplicating client and assignment details into every intake object could consume substantial memory.

A better approach would be to read eligible active intakes in batches, then fetch the related client and assignment records for each batch. Each workflow item would carry only the fields needed for processing; PDFs would be loaded when needed.

active_intakes.csv excludes inactive records, but it doesn’t guarantee a small dataset. For this demo, loading everything is a reasonable simplification, and we should label it as such.

Assistant

Yes—250 clients is comfortably manageable for this approach, assuming the JSON contains text fields, filenames, assignments, and flags, rather than embedded PDF contents.

At an illustrative 5–10 KB per joined intake, the dataset would be roughly 1.25–2.5 MB before runtime overhead. Loading and joining that in n8n is reasonable.

My production-scale concern was overstated for your expected workload. The shared dataset approach fits this demo and that scale.

Assistant

I’ll check n8n’s current Compose and environment-variable settings, then give you the file contents, paths, and commands. I won’t create files or run Docker.

Assistant

Use n8n_work as the Compose project directory, with persistent data under storage. Docker Desktop can still supply the Docker engine on Windows; you’ll manage this installation through PowerShell.

This sets the installation’s project directory, rather than changing Docker’s global storage location. I haven’t created or changed any files.

1. Folder layout

Create this structure:

D:\lawfirm-intake-project\project\
├── resources\
└── n8n_work\
    ├── compose.yaml
    ├── openai-key.txt
    ├── openai-key.example.txt
    ├── .gitignore
    └── storage\
        ├── n8n\
        └── files\
  • storage/n8n: n8n database, credentials, settings, and encryption key.
  • storage/files: generated briefs, emails, and other workflow output.
  • The existing resources folder will also be accessible inside the container.

2. Create compose.yaml

Write this to:

D:\lawfirm-intake-project\project\n8n_work\compose.yaml

name: lawfirm-n8n

services:
  n8n:
    image: n8nio/n8n:latest
    restart: unless-stopped

    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5678:5678"

    env_file:
      - ./openai-key.txt

    environment:
      TZ: America/New_York
      GENERIC_TIMEZONE: America/New_York

      N8N_HOST: localhost
      N8N_PORT: "5678"
      N8N_PROTOCOL: http
      N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL: http://localhost:5678/
      WEBHOOK_URL: http://localhost:5678/

      N8N_ENFORCE_SETTINGS_FILE_PERMISSIONS: "true"

      # Allow workflow expressions to reference OPENAI_API_KEY.
      N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE: "false"

      # Allow file nodes to access the mounted workflow directories.
      N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO: /files
      N8N_BLOCK_FILE_ACCESS_TO_N8N_FILES: "true"

    volumes:
      - type: bind
        source: ./storage/n8n
        target: /home/node/.n8n

      - type: bind
        source: ./storage/files
        target: /files/output

      - type: bind
        source: ../resources
        target: /files/resources

The resources mount is writable because your workflow updates CSV flags. The original_resources backup is not mounted.

The environment-access setting allows expressions to read environment variables; use this configuration for your own local demo workflows. n8n configuration reference

3. Create the private key file

Write this to:

D:\lawfirm-intake-project\project\n8n_work\openai-key.txt

OPENAI_API_KEY=replace-with-your-actual-openai-api-key

Despite its .txt extension, this file uses NAME=value syntax. Compose reads it using env_file and injects the value into the container environment. Docker environment-file documentation

Create a second file, openai-key.example.txt, containing only:

OPENAI_API_KEY=replace-with-your-openai-api-key

Commit the example file to GitHub; keep the real key file private. This excludes the secret rather than merely obscuring it.

4. Create .gitignore

Write this to:

D:\lawfirm-intake-project\project\n8n_work\.gitignore

# Local API key
/openai-key.txt

# n8n database, credentials, settings, and generated output
/storage/

These rules apply to files that haven’t already been tracked by Git.

5. Run these PowerShell commands

Make sure Docker Desktop is running with Linux containers, then:

Set-Location 'D:\lawfirm-intake-project\project\n8n_work'

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path .\storage\n8n, .\storage\files

docker version
docker compose version

docker compose config --quiet
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps

Open http://localhost:5678 and complete the initial account setup.

To view logs:

docker compose logs --tail 100 -f n8n

Press Ctrl+C to stop following logs; the container keeps running.

To stop or restart the installation:

docker compose stop
docker compose start

6. Use the key and files in n8n

Setting OPENAI_API_KEY does not automatically configure an OpenAI node. When creating its OpenAI credential, switch the API Key field to an expression and enter:

{{ $env.OPENAI_API_KEY }}

Use container paths in file nodes:

/files/resources/active_intakes.csv
/files/resources/clients.csv
/files/resources/lawclerk_assignments.csv
/files/resources/paralegal_assignments.csv

/files/output/

After changing openai-key.txt, recreate the container so it receives the updated environment:

docker compose up -d --force-recreate n8n

you skipped the docker part and went right to composer, I wanted to start docker from powershell

Assistant

You’re right—I skipped starting Docker itself.

On Windows, Docker Desktop runs the Docker engine. Start it from PowerShell:

Start-Process -FilePath 'C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe' -WindowStyle Hidden

Give it time to initialize, then check:

docker version

When the output includes both Client and Server, the engine is ready. If it reports a connection error, wait briefly and run the check again.

Then move to your installation directory and start n8n using the files described above:

Set-Location 'D:\lawfirm-intake-project\project\n8n_work'

docker compose up -d

Docker starts the engine; docker compose up -d starts your n8n container.

Add a Code node after Extract From File.

Set Language to JavaScript and Mode to Run Once for All Items. Paste:

const tables = {
  clients: new Map(),
  intakes: new Map(),
  clerks: new Map(),
  paralegals: new Map(),
};

const has = (record, field) =>
  Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(record, field);

for (const item of $input.all()) {
  const record = { ...item.json };

  // Convert CSV flag strings into JSON booleans.
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(record)) {
    if (value === 'true') record[key] = true;
    if (value === 'false') record[key] = false;
  }

  // Identify the source table using its distinct fields.
  let table;

  if (has(record, 'intake_id')) {
    table = tables.intakes;

    for (const field of [
      'document_filenames',
      'expected_document_types',
    ]) {
      record[field] = (record[field] ?? '')
        .split('|')
        .map(value => value.trim())
        .filter(Boolean);
    }
  } else if (has(record, 'first_name')) {
    table = tables.clients;
  } else if (has(record, 'intake_brief_created')) {
    table = tables.clerks;
  } else if (has(record, 'research_memorandum_status')) {
    table = tables.paralegals;
  } else {
    throw new Error('Unrecognized CSV record');
  }

  if (!record.contact_id || table.has(record.contact_id)) {
    throw new Error(
      `Missing or duplicate contact_id: ${record.contact_id}`
    );
  }

  table.set(record.contact_id, record);
}

// Only active intake records drive the output.
return [...tables.intakes.values()].map(intake => {
  const contactId = intake.contact_id;
  const client = tables.clients.get(contactId);
  const clerk = tables.clerks.get(contactId);
  const paralegal = tables.paralegals.get(contactId);

  if (!client || !clerk || !paralegal) {
    throw new Error(`Missing related record for ${contactId}`);
  }

  return {
    json: {
      contact_id: contactId,
      client,
      intake,
      clerk_assignment: clerk,
      paralegal_assignment: paralegal,
    },
  };
});

Click Execute step. Expect 2 items, each containing the four nested records.

Then connect a Loop Over Items node and set Batch Size to 1. Its loop output will feed the intake-processing steps; its done output runs after all intakes finish.

const intake = $json.intake;

const receivedTypes = new Set(
  intake.document_filenames.map(filename =>

      .replace(`${intake.intake_id}-`, '')

);
